One Page Rules Grimdark Future Scale for 3D Printing

Grimdark Future is a free ruleset that leans heavily on 3D printing, so its community sends out a lot of STL proxies. It rides the common 32mm heroic band, which makes matching your files to their built baseline the main job.

Grimdark Future has no official miniature range — it is designed to work with whatever you own. The 32mm recommendation aligns with modern Games Workshop and the majority of 3D printed STL files. The game's flexibility makes it the most accessible entry point for players with custom-printed collections.

Publisher: One Page Rules·Base Sizes: 25mm, 32mm, 40mm, 50mm, 60mm, 80mm, 100mm, 120mm

Because the game is system-agnostic and players bring whatever they printed, I just keep everything at a clean 32mm heroic baseline. Most community STLs land there already, so the regular win is verifying the eye line rather than performing an exotic conversion.

The variety of sculptors means baseline drift is the real issue. I measure every STL on import rather than trusting the file name, and I scale anything that drifts back to 32mm before it sits on the table next to the rest of the army.

Deep Dive: The 32mm rule-agnostic playground

Grimdark Future has no official range — it is built for printed and proxy collections. That means you set the scale, and the only rule that matters is keeping one scale across your whole force.

No Official Range, No Wrong Answer

Grimdark Future is miniature-agnostic by design — it works with whatever you own. The 32mm recommendation aligns with modern Games Workshop and the majority of 3D printed STL files, but a 28mm classic collection works just as well. What the rules actually care about is base sizes, not model heights.

Pick a Standard for Your Army

Conversion Formula Slicer %
Classic (28mm) → GDF standard (32mm)32 ÷ 28114.3%
GDF standard (32mm) → Classic (28mm)28 ÷ 3287.5%

Commit to one lane for the whole army. The only real scale mistake in this game is switching mid-force.

Base Sizes Drive the Rules

Grimdark Future's unit categories are keyed to base sizes — infantry, heavy infantry, cavalry, and so on. The game is forgiving about visual consistency precisely because the bases do the rules work. Print your models to fit the correct base category and the army plays correctly even if the sculpts vary.

FDM Settings

Since there are no official models to match, print whatever you want. I use a 0.2mm nozzle at 0.06mm layers for characters and a 0.4mm nozzle at 0.1mm for rank-and-file. PLA with high fan from the first few layers gives clean overhangs on capes and weapon barrels.

Common Grimdark Future Mistakes

  • Mixing 28mm and 32mm mid-army. The rules do not care, but the table will look inconsistent. Pick one lane.
  • Ignoring the base size chart. It drives the rules — a proxy on the wrong base category changes how it plays.
  • Over-investing in rank-and-file detail. Across-the-table models read fine at 0.1mm. Spend detail on heroes and monsters.

Printing these minis on FDM

Print at a 0.4mm nozzle and 0.08mm layers for rank-and-file, finer for characters. Verify every community STL's eye line on import and scale to 32mm for a coherent force.

All settings tested on my Bambu Lab A1 Mini with PLA. Your printer may want something different — always print a test piece first.

Frequently Asked Questions

What scale is Grimdark Future?
Grimdark Future uses a 32mm heroic baseline, matching modern Warhammer 40k.
Why do my community proxies not match?
Different sculptors drift from 32mm. Measure each STL's eye line on import and scale it back to 32mm.
